# Chapter 21 — Certified Random Numbers and Channel Audit: Min-Entropy with a Credible Interval and Block Drift in m-qg {#sec-qjax21 .unnumbered}

> **Analysis and update date:** November 23, 2026

## 21.1 Point versus certificate

$H_{\min}=-\log_2\frac{1+|qg_Z|}{2}$ (Ch. 19) evaluated at the **point** $\hat{qg}_Z=2k_0/N-1$ overestimates: with $k_0=N/2$ it gives $1.000$ bit for any $N$. The certified version takes the maximum of $|qg_Z|$ over the $99.8\%$ central credible interval ($0.1\%$ tail on each side) of the Bayes–Haar posterior $\mathrm{Beta}(1+k_0,1+N-k_0)$ (Ch. 8):
$$H_{\min}^{\text{cert}}=-\log_2\frac{1+\max(|qg_Z^{\text{lo}}|,|qg_Z^{\text{hi}}|)}{2}:\quad N=10^3\to0.866,\ 10^4\to0.956,\ 10^5\to0.986,\ 10^6\to0.9955\ \text{bit}.$$
Budget to certify $H_{\min}\ge0.99$ ($|qg_Z|\le7.0$ m-qg with $0.1\%$ tails): $N\approx1.97\cdot10^5$ shots (`exact` for the i.i.d. model). With a real bias of $30$ m-qg ($N=2\cdot10^5$): point $0.9528$, certified $0.9431$, true $0.9574$ — the certificate is a lower bound.

## 21.2 Channel audit: stationarity of qgZ by blocks

$\chi^2$ of homogeneity of $p_0$ between blocks of $10^4$ ($19$ d.o.f.): stationary channel $27.1$; linear drift from $0\to80$ m-qg: $130.7$, with per-block readings $+7,-32,-22,-49,-71$ m-qg. The drift invalidates the i.i.d. hypothesis of §21.1 before the point value shows it (`exact` statistical). Toeplitz extraction and CHSH arithmetic are checked in `tools/verify_cap21.py`; Trevisan and device-independent certification are referenced (§41, §42), not reproduced.

A $2\times B$ homogeneity table has $B-1$ degrees of freedom; with $B=20$ blocks there are $19$. Rejecting homogeneity ($130.7$ versus $27.1$) diagnoses drift but does not identify its cause or certify cryptographic randomness. Trevisan and device-independent certification therefore stay referenced and marked `unverified` here: `bell_chsh` only evaluates already-measured correlations and does not accredit space-like separation or free choice of settings. Toeplitz extraction and CHSH arithmetic are `exact` within the audited i.i.d. model.

## 21.5 Verification — `tools/verify_cap21.py`

```
[1] N=    10000, k0=N/2: point H_min = 1.0000 | 99.8% central interval qg_Z = [-30.9, +30.9] m-qg | cert H_min = 0.9561 bit
[2] H_min ≥ 0.99 certified: |qg_Z| ≤ 7.0 m-qg ⇒ N ≈ 197358 shots
[3] real bias 30 m-qg, N=2e5: point H_min=0.9528, cert=0.9431, true=0.9574
[4] χ²(19 d.o.f.): stationary 27.1 | drift 130.7
[5] Toeplitz: y=T x mod 2 with T 128×512; linear and reproducible with seed=7; output [1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1]... (exact)
[6] CHSH: S=E00+E01+E10−E11; local |S|≤2, quantum |S|=2.8284=2√2 (exact arithmetic); DI and Trevisan out of scope
verify_cap21: OK
```
The reproducible validation of this review is `verify_cap21: OK`: cert$(10^6)>0.99$, cert$(10^3)<0.9$; certificate $\le$ true value with a $30$ m-qg bias; $\chi^2_{\text{drift}}>3\chi^2_{\text{stat}}$; Toeplitz linear and reproducible; CHSH respects the local bound and reaches $2\sqrt2$; `tests/test_qrng.py` passes with `4 passed`.

Asserts: cert$(10^6)>0.99$, cert$(10^3)<0.9$; cert $\le$ true with bias; $\chi^2_{\text{drift}}>3\chi^2_{\text{stat}}$; $T[1:,1:]=T[:-1,:-1]$ and $T(x\oplus y)=Tx\oplus Ty$; $|S|>2$ only if the input correlations allow it.
